title: Area chart
description: Filled areas that show a volume over time: smooth by default, overlapping, stacked into a total or as 100% shares. Hover to read every series at one x; zoom with Ctrl / ⌘ + wheel or a pinch.

props.name: series
props.description: Series drawn as areas unless they set a `type`

props.name: curve
props.description: Shape of the edges: straight, smooth (monotone) or steps

props.name: stacked
props.description: Stacks the areas on top of each other

props.name: percent
props.description: Scales the stacks to 100% (implies `stacked`)

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the chart (the legend included); numbers are pixels

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the chart; numbers are pixels

props.name: xAxis
props.description: X axis

props.name: yAxis
props.description: Y axis

props.name: renderer
props.description: Backend of the data layer: `auto` tries WebGPU, then WebGL2, then WebGL, then Canvas2D

props.name: legend
props.description: Legend; shown by default when several series have a name

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Tooltip; `false` disables it

props.name: crosshair
props.description: Vertical guide line following the pointer

props.name: annotations
props.description: Background areas and reference lines

props.name: interaction
props.description: Zoom (Ctrl / ⌘ + wheel, pinch), pan (drag), double-click reset and keyboard navigation; `false` makes the chart static

props.name: padding
props.description: Space around the plot area, in pixels

props.name: palette
props.description: Series colors (defaults to the `--chart-series-1..8` CSS variables, then the theme colors)

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the chart

props.name: locale
props.description: Locale of the texts and numbers the chart writes (tooltip rows, compact units `k` / `万`, separators, month and weekday names of time axes)

props.name: labels
props.description: Overrides of the built-in texts of the `locale`

props.name: renderTooltip
props.description: React content of the tooltip (replaces the default content)

events.name: onHover
events.description: Called when the hovered (or keyboard-focused) points change

events.name: onPointClick
events.description: Called when a point (or bar) is clicked

events.name: onPlotClick
events.description: Called when the plot area is clicked where there is no point

events.name: onZoom
events.description: Called when the user zooms or pans

events.name: onRendererChange
events.description: Called with the backend once it is ready (and when it falls back after a GPU loss)

examples.title: Basic
examples.description: One series over Date x values: the edge is a smooth (monotone) curve that never overshoots the data.

examples.title: Cumulative vs plan
examples.description: Running total of sales against an evenly growing plan drawn as a line series; null values leave the months still to come empty.

examples.title: Capacity forecast
examples.description: Disk usage as an area and a line series extending the trend of the last 30 days up to the capacity, marked by a y annotation; a rect shades the future and the readout gives the day the volume fills up.

examples.title: Energy mix
examples.description: Electricity generation by source over a day, stacked: the top edge is the total demand and the solar bump shows when the other sources ramp down. Each series sets its own color.

examples.title: Readout panel
examples.description: tooltip={false} with crosshair and onHover: a side panel lists the headcount of every department at the hovered month, largest first, and shows the latest month when the pointer leaves.

examples.title: Mirrored in / out
examples.description: Download above zero and upload below it on the same scale, a common layout for network monitoring; the y format drops the sign.

examples.title: 100% stacked
examples.description: percent scales every x to 100% to compare shares rather than amounts, such as a market share; the tooltip shows each value and its share.

examples.title: Stacked
examples.description: stacked piles the areas so the top edge is the total; use it when the parts add up to a meaningful whole. Click a legend item to hide a source and restack the others.

examples.title: Step
examples.description: curve="step" holds each value until the next one, which suits counts that change at discrete moments; an annotation marks the quota.

examples.title: Year over year
examples.description: Last year's season drawn as a faint grey area behind this year's, on the same calendar days; text annotations name the spikes and an x line marks the last shipping day before Christmas.

examples.title: Total of the visible range
examples.description: onZoom reports the visible x range after every zoom and pan: the readout sums the solar energy of the days in view. The button calls resetZoom() on the chart ref.

AreaChartProps.series: Series drawn as areas unless they set a type
AreaChartProps.stacked: Stacks the areas on top of each other
AreaChartProps.percent: Scales the stacks to 100% at each x (implies stacked)

stacked.title: Stacked areas
stacked.description: Three traffic sources piled up with smooth edges (the default curve).

percent.title: 100% stacked
percent.description: percent scales every stack to 100%: the share of each energy source through the day, with straight edges.

props.height: Height of the chart, the legend included: pixels or any CSS length
props.options: Other engine options (axes, legend, tooltip, palette, format…) merged with the element's own properties; property only
props.instance: The engine instance (minerva-design/charts/core), null until the element is rendered and connected

events.minerva-hover: The hovered (or keyboard-focused) points changed; detail: { x, xLabel, items }, null when nothing is hovered
events.minerva-point-click: A point or a bar was clicked; detail: { x, xLabel, items }
events.minerva-plot-click: The plot area was clicked where there is no point; detail: { x, y } in data coordinates
events.minerva-zoom: The user zoomed or panned; detail: { x, y } (the visible ranges)
events.minerva-renderer-change: The backend is ready, or fell back after a GPU loss; detail: { renderer }

methods.getView: Visible range, null before the engine is created
methods.getRenderer: Backend in use (webgpu, webgl2, webgl, canvas2d), null until ready
